title: Left slice density bounded by the derivative of the distribution function, for a finite measure on any measurable space (Simon 6.4.9–4.10, used in 6.5.1 (10))
statement: Let α be a measurable space (a type α : Type with a σ-algebra, given by the instance [MeasurableSpace α]), let μ be a finite measure on α (IsFiniteMeasure μ), let f : α → ℝ be measurable and let t ∈ ℝ. Put F(s) := (μ({x ∈ α : f(x) < s})).toReal for s ∈ ℝ, the distribution function of f under μ, read in ℝ. If F is differentiable at t, then liminf_{h → 0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({x : t − h < f(x) < t}) ≤ ofReal(F′(t)). Here F′ = deriv F, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, values lie in [0, ∞], and the liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of right neighbourhoods of 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (α : Type) [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ) (t : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasure μ → Measurable f → DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s : ℝ => (μ {x | f x < s}).toReal) t → liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (deriv (fun s : ℝ => (μ {x | f x < s}).toReal) t)
